recipes.name: Kelly's Slow Cooker Beef, Mushroom, and Barley Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds beef sirloin, cut into chunks
0.25 teaspoon garlic salt, or to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Season beef with garlic salt, salt, and pepper.

Place seasoned beef into a slow cooker with stock, tomato sauce, water, barley, carrots, mushrooms, onion, garlic, and bay leaves. Stir to combine, then cover and cook on Low until soup thickens and beef is tender, about 6 hours.

review.reviewBody: A very hearty satisfying soup! I made this soup with things on hand. I was concerned that some reviewers said that the soup had "no flavor" so I went a little heavier on the onions (one medium) and 2 more cloves of garlic as well as adding a 1/4 tsp of black pepper. I did use left over tomato sauce from a jar probably closer to 2 cups, and since I didn't have any beef stock on hand I used Knorr beef bullion for the equivalent of the 32 ounces . I pre- browned my beef seasoned with garlic pepper and onion powder (only had a a little over a pound) and used 2x's the mushrooms, (baby portabellas). Finally added a 1/4 cup Brandy (instead of wine) into the mix . The end result was a fabulous rich and flavorful soup. I will definitely make this again .

A very good, hearty stew. I leave out the carrots (can't stand cooked carrots) and tend to double the mushrooms (one pack white button and one pack portabella) but that's just personal tastes. I've also successfully substituted basic stew meat for lower costs, but that definitely makes for a 'put on at 6AM and cook on low for 12 hours' kind of setup for the meat to come out tender.

This recipe is a good start. The pictures shows more of a brothy stew. The barley starches actually make this a very pasty stew. This can be addressed by cooking the barley separately and rinsing it to remove the starches. Add the barley in at the end of the cooking. A dash of Worcestershire sauce adds some flavor. I also added a cup of frozen peas as well.

I actually made this on the stove top, so I sauteed the beef and then added the vegetables to saute for a bit before adding everything else. I made a double batch and found that doubling the barley made it much to thick and I had to add more beef stock, but it was unbelievably delicious. I will definitely make again!

This was pretty good. I think I would have liked it better if I had browned the meat first. I added a teaspoon of Old Bay seasoning. Also, a dietitian friend said not to add starches to a crockpot until near the end of cooking time so I added the barley with an hour left to cook.

The soup was delicious. I followed the recipe with some minor additions based on some of the reviews. I waited to add the barley till there was 2 hrs of cooking time left. It was done in an effort to keep the barley from absorbing all the broth. Added a pack of Extra Beefy Lipton Onion Soup Mix, Worcestershire sauce, and some red pepper flakes all for flavor. Served with shredded Swiss cheese melted on top and a crusty sour dough bread I would not hesitate to make this again
Yum! Added worshchester, red wine, doubled the mushrooms. Used quick barley at the end to not over cook in the slow cooker.

I find the tomato soup to be a bit off putting and sweet, so I use about 1/2 cup of split peas & other spices to kick it up a bit. I also use beef shank or beef neck bones to add additional flavor. Cook the bones until the meat basically falls off the bone. Delicious!
I have a small crock pot and wanted to increase the veggies, so I used half the amount of beef and roughly chopped a fennel bulb to add. Also tasty, I stirred in some fresh thyme sprigs to the mix :)

This is a very hearty soup! I thought it was a little bland, so I added 1 T Worcester sauce, 1 t each of beef and mushroom "Better Than Bouillon" and 1/4 C red wine. Delicious paired with a crusty roll and red wine.

Instead of one full cup of water, I used 1/2 cup water and 1/2 cup red wine. I used 8oz baby bella mushrooms, instead of 6oz, and served with cracked salt and pepper on top, and with crusty bread. Delicious!

I followed the recipe to the T. Not a soup ... a mushy stew in retrospect. The cooking time turned the meat to the mush I refer to. Not the beef barley soup I had in mind. I won't make this again. Very large quantity of leftovers to dispose of.
Very easy and awesome recipe. Thanks for sharing
It was delicious! Kept recipe pretty much as is. Just used a whole onion, a little celery and substituted the carrots with parsnips. Very thick and hearty.

It’s not a traditional mushroom barley soup and ended up tasting more like a tomato soup. The barley was too much and ended up soaking up all the broth after the first day and the carrots did not get close to soft enough. Next time I will be using a different recipe.
This is, by far, my favorite beef barley soup. I double the mushrooms because I'm a mushroom lover!
Not enough flavor for my husband and I. Cooked a little over 6 hours but carrots were still crisp and meat was not too too tender. I will stick to my own version.
Made per the recipe, however used 8oz of mushrooms and 2 good tbsp of Worcestershire sauce plus 2-3 sticks chopped celery. Pearl Barley worked well for me! Hot buttered bread for 'dunking' Yummy!!
